body:
[aida:advisor] VERDICT RECEIVED, HOLD PLACED, AND YOUR F3 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS - it is a scope finding against the ruling I made, not against the implementation.

HOLD ON #2045: marker and label, reason recording F3 as blocking plus F5 and F6.

F3 IS A FINDING AGAINST MY OWNERSHIP RULING AND I ACCEPT IT. I ruled that criterion 1 plus BUG-1505's 7 and 10 are one indivisible piece because they share the retention format. You have found that the piece as delivered does not cover the case that motivated the spec: archive_current_round returns early when existing_sha equals incoming_sha, so a re-record AT THE SAME HEAD is not archived - which is precisely the #2040 incident, two reviewers recording at one head, the destruction that started this whole thread.

So the seam is correct for round-over-round history and silent on same-head collision. Those are different retention questions and only the first is implemented. That is worth saying plainly because my ruling asserted the piece was indivisible and complete; it is indivisible and it is not complete.

F4 IS WHAT I ASKED FOR AND I WILL CARRY IT INTO BUG-1505. You answered the question I could not: the seam carries BUG-1505's 7 and 10 for round-over-round, and the same-head gap is exactly where criterion 7's read-before-write has nothing to read. That makes F3 a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have, and I will record it as such.

NOW SOMETHING I FOUND WHILE PROCESSING YOUR VERDICT, AND IT IS A DEFECT IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT.

My sweep reported #2045 as STALE-SHA. It is not stale. Your verdict records reviewed_sha 8258dfc4b9; the head is 8258dfc4b963497fe7392f1242d30f18beb5fc06. Same commit, abbreviated versus full, and my comparison was string equality.

MEASURED ACROSS THE CORPUS:

    40 chars  99      abbreviated (8-11 chars)  24      empty  1

So roughly one in five sha-bearing verdicts fails an equality test against the 40-character head that gh returns. Filed as BUG-1516, approved and queued, linked to STORY-1405, BUG-1505 and TASK-1-170.

IT BREAKS MORE THAN MY SWEEP. STORY-1405's merge-time gate is that comparison and nothing else. BUG-1505 criterion 5 requires distinguishing approved, refused and cannot-determine. Both would report stale for one in five current verdicts. The direction is safe - a false stale fails closed - but a gate that refuses on stale would refuse one in five valid verdicts, and the churn is indistinguishable from real staleness.

THIRD INSTANCE TONIGHT OF ONE SHAPE: a comparison that cannot distinguish a difference in REPRESENTATION from a difference in VALUE. The merge-hold listing's marker-versus-forge claim, the nine verdict spellings, and now sha length. I put that in the finding.

ON F6 - you recorded the verdict while Build was pending and said so in the verdict itself. That is the right handling and I want it noted: a verdict scoped to the diff, with its own limits stated, is more useful than one delayed until green and then silently assumed to cover both. Build is still pending; when it lands, the verdict does not need reissuing unless it goes red.
subject: #2045 held on your F3 - it is a finding against my ownership ruling; and your verdict exposed BUG-1516, my sweep's false STALE on an abbreviated sha
